rationale_evidence.anchor: Decision support capability does not automatically imply decision authority.
rationale_evidence.statement: A 1998 source claim that computers can shape aims, provide/evaluate information and present options but do not possess the value judgment required for a 'true decision' is explicitly NOT imported as a KnowledgeOS truth (flagged as a dated philosophical/managerial position), but the underlying architectural insight is kept: decision support capability does not automatically imply decision authority; an AI Agent may discover/analyse evidence, generate/evaluate alternatives, recommend, and simulate consequences, without exercising a DecisionRight unless governance explicitly grants it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge answers "is this justified?" Governance answers "who may choose?" Decision answers "what was chosen?"
rationale_evidence.statement: Two orthogonal kernel axes identified: Epistemic axis ('can we justify this?': Question/Evidence/Reasoning/Inference/Claim/Assessment) and Decisional axis ('may we choose this?': Aim/Alternative/DecisionRight/DecisionalSpace/Constraint/Risk/DecisionReadiness/Decision/Accountability), intersecting via Knowledge->informs->DecisionBasis->DecisionAuthority->exercises->Decision; proposed as a candidate central architectural principle: Knowledge answers 'is this justified?', Governance answers 'who may choose?', Decision answers 'what was chosen?'.
